title: What the counting block learned stays learned
intention: The counting block keeps an append-only ledger of every clear it has applied, in its own instance-space beside table.json, and folds that ledger together with the live clears on every compile, so a row once taught stays taught when the trouble that taught it is re-raised or expires.
why: Measured 2026-10-12: cairn/machines/counting_block/block.py compile() derives every row increment from the clears the trouble device serves NOW (_ask_clears). A re-raise of a CLEARED trouble starts a fresh ticket with cleared_by [] (cairn/devices/trouble/trouble.py:271), so Akien's clears on who-writes-what-cairncommons-troubles-raise-gate, -troubles-clear-gate and -tickets-append-cc (present at CairnCommons 3113bb7) vanished from the live store before 4f8d11706516 could class them, and those rows can never learn. And per Akien's 2026-10-11 spec troubles are logging artifacts deleted after 30 days, so every taught row would un-learn within a month.
traces_to: Law 1 (a settled answer is not re-asked: a row Akien taught must not raise again) and Law 3 (the learned count is kept with its measured provenance).
how: cairn/machines/counting_block/block.py only: pulse() reads taught.json (beside table.json under table_dir(); absent = []), unions it with the rows _ask_clears returns (key: id+at+hand_class; dedupe), passes the union to compile() as clears (compile stays pure), and after compiling appends to taught.json (atomic, via _atomic) every akien-class clear that compile() recorded in increments and the ledger lacks. Only akien-class clears enter the ledger. Deleting taught.json returns to today's behaviour; deleting table.json still recompiles byte-identically given the same ledger. Update the module docstring's THREE FILES paragraph to four.
falsifier: cairn/machines/counting_block/proofs/test_a_taught_row_stays_taught.py under PROVES {'01d34298ecae': {'1','2','3'}}: (1) a pulse over a scratch world where an akien clear teaches a row, then a second pulse where ask() no longer returns that clear: the row's count is unchanged and no raise is reported for it; (2) a cc-class clear never enters taught.json; (3) with taught.json deleted, a pulse equals today's behaviour (the row drops back). Hollow: today's pulse reds 1. In the world: once Akien clears a who-writes-what row from his terminal, its taught.json line survives the next re-raise.
